[[Image:cogwheel-5.svg|thumb|link=|'''gau ko la lojban cu me lo bangu pe do'''<br>The symbol of The Crash Course: nature and logic]]{{La Bangu/en}}
'''The Crash Course method''' is a new method of teaching Lojban that:
#uses a simple style of speaking Lojban with fewer compound words ([[lujvo]]), more usage examples and answers to "How to say ..." questions.
#uses terminology taken from the language the learner uses from birth.
#*This principle brings Lojban to people, not drags people into Lojban. It adapts the teaching method to the language the student uses in everyday life. Thus, this method is flexible and doesn't have universal recommendations. It all depends on whom you teach.
#*For example, for speakers of English (and most languages of Europe) The Crash Course method calls [[brivla]] "verbs", calls [[sumti]] "nouns". Although, such terms as "noun" and "verb" can mean different things in different languages and are not precise terms they are fine for initial explanation of how Lojban works.
#carefully selects new rules and lexicon being introduced into the language compared to Standard Lojban (which is described in [[CLL|Complete Lojban Grammar]] and extended or modified by [[BPFK]] decrees). As of now ~2/3 of these new rules are just an application of [[zasni gerna cenba vreji|zasni gerna]] first proposed by [[User:Xorxes|la xorxes]]. ~1/3 is just reflection of live usage if Lojban + other optimizations of the grammar. In the first place only those rules are described in The Crash Course that are already popular in the <u>active</u> Lojban community. Important note: these differences may not be official and thus not form a part of Standard Lojban.

<!--Unlike some splinter proposals by [[la xorxes]] and several other Lojbanists -->The Crash Course tries to preserve the current state of the language as much as possible if this state produces a learnable and usable language.

[[La Bangu: ilmentufa|ilmentufa]] syntactical parser is to be used for The Crash Course.

===The Crash Course - The realization of Lojban. Learning resources.===
[[User:Gleki|La Gleki]] started developing a large project: ''[[The Crash Course in Lojban: The Journey]]''.

Two of it's important parts are:
#“[[L17-01|The La Gleki's Crash Course (CC)]]”. It teaches basic Lojban to beginners.
#“[[ELG|Extended Lojbanic Grammar (ELG)]]”. It's based on CLL and is intended for those who've read The Crash Course and now want more. ELG is to be written in simple Lojban.

==Conflicts with CLL Lojban that break past usage==
Some parts of what is explained by The Crash Course resources can be incompatible with Standard Lojban and thus considered not a part of Lojban. Here are the differences from Standard Lojban (that conflict with what is described in CLL):
*Any errata<ref>[[CLL, aka Reference Grammar, Errata]]</ref><ref>[[Suggestions for CLL, second edition]]</ref><ref>[[CLL, aka Reference Grammar, Errata]]</ref> found in CLL are fixed.
**E.g. '''vo'a''' series is used to refer back to corresponding parts of the sentence, not bridi. '''lo nei''', '''lo SE nei''' is used to refer to parts of the current [[bridi]].
*[[How to use xorlo|xorlo]]<nowiki/>fication except '''le'''. '''le''' is used in [[Keith Donnellan|referential]] sense.
*[[The Dot Side]] applied.
*[[cmevla]] is a class of [[brivla|verbs]], so you can say '''i la moxamed morsi cu jmive'''. So those who earlier used CLL Lojban please don't forget to place '''cu''' after names and before [[selbri]] (verb relations) to make your phrases valid in both variations of the language.
*'''lu''' is so powerful, if used without '''li'u''' it scans the text for the grammar to be broken and puts '''li'u''' automatically at the point the grammar breaks thus trying to restore correctness. As all those differences (including below) make many more constructs grammatically correct, we can say that many more sentences with '''lu''' but not '''li'u''' can get a new meaning. Thus it is advised not to omit '''li'u'''.
It's advisable to read old texts and correct them so that are valid both in standard Lojban and in The Crash Course.

# Does '''le''' need to be replaced with '''lo'''? It's not a problem of matching '''le''' with RegExp (/\ble\b/g) in the source code of ELG but what function should '''le''' have in The Crash Course? If it's useless then why not retain it as a synonym of '''lo''' (and in this case it's a pity xorlo replaced one word with another when it should have just changed the philosophy/definitions behind them). Alternatively '''le''' is mapped to referentiality from [[Keith Donnellan]]'s philosophy.

==Differences from zasni gerna proposed by xorxes==
Compared to [[zasni gerna cenba vreji|zasni gerna]] first proposed by [[User:Xorxes|la xorxes]] The Crash Course has the following differences. For other differences from Standard Lojban see the section above.
* '''sa''' is not removed as it has many uses
* [https://groups.google.com/d/topic/lojban/ExtEumbYoQg/discussion Connective unification] is not a reform anymore but rather a new preferred style retaining all past usage. Unlike xorxe's mad proposals no cmavo is removed from the language. E.g. the class A is just a synonym of JA. It will eliminate breaking past usage for connective system (A and ZIhE are not removed from the language, they are presented as some trends in modern deviations from Standard Lojban).
* numbers removed from the grammar but preprocessed 1=>pa, 2=>re and so on granting l33t style official status (within the frame of The Crash Course) (see [[Stub: L33t gismu]]).
* CMENE renamed to CMEVLA

== Philosophical aspects ==
Lojban had multiple words to denote the same operator: "logical AND". Indeed, there were '''je''', '''.e''', '''gi'e''', '''gu'e''', '''zi'e'''. Almost the same for other logical operators (for joining relative clauses there was only '''zi'e''', though).

Now we have one word for that: '''je''' (retaining other words for backward compatibility). Which is great.
